title: An inverse limit of flat modules over the quotients A/I^n is flat over a Noetherian A
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Let $(M_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an inverse system of $A$-modules, with $A$-linear transition maps $M_{n+1}\to M_n$, such that (1) for every $n$, $I^nM_n=0$ and $M_n$ is a flat $A/I^n$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and (2) every transition map $M_{n+1}\to M_n$ is surjective. Let $M=\varprojlim_nM_n$ (compatible sequences $(x_n)_n$, $x_n\in M_n$, with componentwise $A$-module structure). Then $M$ is a flat $A$-module, and for every finitely generated $A$-module $Q$ the canonical map $Q\otimes_AM\to\varprojlim_nQ\otimes_AM_n$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0912 (lemma-limit-flat, line 6475); its proof uses Lemma Tag 0911 (lemma-tor-strictly-pro-zero, line 6449), Homology Lemma Tag 070E (homology-lemma-apply-Mittag-Leffler-again) and Algebra Lemma Tag 00HD (lemma-flat)

proof.text: Use Artin--Rees in the presentation-level kernel lemma to obtain, for every finite P and K ⊆ P, eventual vanishing of the kernel of K ⊗ M_m → P ⊗ M_m under transition to any fixed n.

Apply the general finite tensor comparison criterion to the surjective tower and the kernel-vanishing result of Step 1. This proves the stated injectivity and surjectivity onto compatible families for every finite Q, with the canonical projection tensors.

Use the finitely generated ideal criterion for flatness. Fix a finitely generated ideal J and y ∈ J ⊗ lim M killed in A ⊗ lim M. Naturality places its m-th coordinate in the tensor kernel of J ↪ A at m. For each n use Step 1 to choose a transition m→n killing that kernel. Compatibility of limit projections identifies its image with the n-th coordinate of y, so all coordinates vanish. Step 2 for J then implies y=0. This proves flatness; Step 2 already proves the tensor clause.
